newsitem.title: HONG KONG: First Tractor seen sizzling on debut.
newsitem.headline: First Tractor seen sizzling on debut.

text.p: Shares of First Tractor Co look set to make a sizzling debut next week as "handover fever" and investors' hopes of hitching a ride on China's growing agricultural sector drives demand, analysts said on Friday.

First Tractor, the largest agricultural tractor maker in China, will float 300 million H-shares or 40 percent of the company in Hong Kong on Monday, just a week before the territory returns to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30.
H-shares are Chinese companies' shares listed in Hong Kong.
"For sure it will benefit from the irrational strength of the market ahead of the handover," said Kinson Au, research manager at Asia Financial Securities.
The blue-chip Hang Seng Index rocketed 4.47 percent to an all-time high of 15,154.36 points on Friday.
"The rally should extend into the handover next week due to handover fever," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas.

But the Hang Seng China Enterprises Index for H-shares eased 0.73 percent to 1,012.55 points as red chips stole the show. The new index for red chips -- Hong Kong-incorporated companies with mainland backing -- rose 2.32 percent to 3,127.87 points.

"Given the good response to its (initial public offering) and its strong background, First Tractor should attract market attention even though it is an H-share company," said Kelvin Tang, an analyst at Impac Asset Managment (HK) Ltd.
First Tractor's Hong Kong public offering of 45 million shares at an issue price of HK$4.50 was 296.4 times subscribed.
Due to the oversubscription, the company reallocated 58.5 million shares from the 255-million-share global placement to the Hong Kong public offer.
Analysts said the share's grey market price was about HK$5.80 on Friday.

"Its fundamentals and concept are strong and it taps the agricultural market in China, which to a certain extent is under the protection of the Chinese government," Au said. "It will benefit from the population growth in the country."
China has at least 1.2 billion people.

Earlier this week, First Tractor chairman Yin Jia Xi said Beijing had introduced a series of policies, including lowering the value-added tax on farm machinery, to help develop the agricultural sector.
First Tractor said it plans to use net proceeds of about HK$1.29 billion to finance expansion of its manufacturing capacity, repay debt and for working capital.
